blockers.finding: The new `user_exit_buffer` minimum is correctly sized in underlying units as the checked sum of separately floored per-position claims, but the gate that consumes it is still the pair-2 mechanism: 'one exact hypothetical stock withdrawal of the buffer from the post-withdraw state'. That single aggregate withdrawal burns `ceil(buffer * Q / b_rate)` b-tokens, which is strictly less than the b-tokens the users themselves burn when they redeem those claims: stock withdraw-all clamps to the position and burns exactly `b_i` (actions.rs:322-325), so the sequential burn is `sum(b_i)`, and `ceil(sum(floor(b_i*r/Q))*Q/r) <= sum(b_i)` with a gap of up to n-1 b-tokens. The check therefore certifies a post-withdraw reserve that is above the strict utilization boundary for the aggregate but below it for the last redeeming user. Reproduced with the frozen smoke script's own `allowed()`: b_rate=1,700,000,000,000, b_supply=5 (vault 2 b-tokens, three users at 1 b-token each), d_supply=1, d_rate=Q, so L=1, S(0)=8, C=7, raw=7 (no donation), claims floor(1.7)=1 each, record=3 (deadline rate equal to live rate). Vault withdrawal x=1 (burn 1) passes every gate (post S=6; hypothetical burn(3)=2 leaves S=3 > 1). Then user1 and user2 withdraw-all succeed (S=5, S=3) but user3's withdraw-all leaves S=1, not > L=1, so stock `require_utilization_below_100` panics (reserve.rs:133-140); a 1-unit partial withdrawal burns the same 1 b-token and also rejects. Without the vault withdrawal all three users exit (S=6,5,3). An exhaustive sweep over d_supply<60, vault<40, n in {2,3,4} at that rate found 4,210 such states. This violates the contract that 'qualification must preserve all still-withdrawable user claims' and ADR0008:284-285 ('any withdrawable unit must exit'); the loss is rounding dust per user, but the whole correction exists to make the gate exact, and the sizing text at 279-285 explicitly rejects 'aggregate-before-floor rounding' while the check re-aggregates.

result.tradeoff_tension: Exact per-user protection versus vault liveness and maintenance: reserving `sum(b_i)` b-tokens reserves every user's full redemption at the strict boundary and needs no rate forecasting, but it withholds slightly more of the vault's exit than the underlying-unit floor sum (users leave zero-unit dust b-tokens), and while any debt remains the vault may be unable to take any tranche until borrowers repay; the alternative of an underlying-unit buffer with a forecasted deadline rate is easier to record in a lineage document but provably under-protects at rounding boundaries and carries an accrual-bound proof obligation per batch.

result.steelman: Strongest case for keeping the underlying-unit hypothetical withdrawal: it reuses the exact stock withdraw arithmetic already differential-tested, keeps the lineage record in the same unit operators reason about, and the residual gap is at most n-1 b-tokens, each worth under one underlying unit, which ADR0008 already discloses as a rounding-loss terminal class. It fails because the ADR's own contract is stronger than 'dust is acceptable': it promises to reserve every still-withdrawable claim and explicitly rejects aggregate-before-floor rounding, and a 1-unit claim that was withdrawable before the vault batch and is not afterwards is a vault-caused user loss, however small. The b-token denomination is strictly simpler: `sum(b_i)` is an integer read from the same inventory, needs no accrual forecast, is monotone nonincreasing after T0 (status 4 blocks supply, ADR0008:53-54; fills and orphaning only move b-tokens away from user classes), and the gate remains one exact stock utilization evaluation.
result.synthesis: Identity matches the refrozen bundle and the delta is confined to replacing the discretionary buffers with an inventory-derived `user_exit_buffer`. The sizing rule is right in kind (complete inventory, per-position floor, conservative deadline rate, block on missing classes or unprovable bound, debt-zero release), the raw/accounting separation from pairs 1-3 is intact, and no raw surplus, donation, backstop credit, market value, or arbitrary number can enlarge the cap. The remaining defect is in the consumer of that buffer: retaining it as one aggregate hypothetical withdrawal under-burns by up to n-1 b-tokens relative to what users actually burn, so the strict utilization boundary is certified for the aggregate but not for the last redeeming user; reproduced concretely with the frozen script's own predicate. Denominating the retained buffer in b-tokens (`sum(b_i)` from the same inventory) closes P3-C1 completely, removes the accrual-forecast obligation from the safety-critical path, and leaves the debt-zero final tranche unchanged. ITERATE on that single correction.
risks: If corrected as required, the deadline-rate bound becomes a record-hygiene input rather than a safety input; the ADR should not let its complexity persist as a perceived invariant.

Vault liveness while debt remains is now fully hostage to user inventory plus borrower-authorized repayment; a serviced tail with many small suppliers can keep the vault at zero tranche until debt-zero, which the plan must disclose to vault holders.

The complete point-read inventory is an off-chain artifact bound into the batch; any indexer gap silently under-counts `B`, so the 'missing positions/classes blocks' rule depends on an authoritative position enumeration (the pool has no on-chain position list), and acceptance should name the enumeration source.
Maintenance: the differential property must now generate multi-user sequential redemption scenarios, not only single aggregate withdrawals, to catch this class of gap on future pins.
file_corrections: ADR0009:281-284: once the gate is b-token denominated, `b_rate_deadline` is only needed for the underlying-unit record used by the raw-sufficiency clause, which pair-2 analysis showed is implied by `R >= C` plus the accounting gate; consider stating that the rate bound is record hygiene, not a withdrawal-cap input, to avoid future readers treating an accrual forecast as an invariant.

ADR0009:477-479: the property text 'one unit below rejects' tests record adequacy only; add the sequential multi-user redemption property (every inventory position can withdraw-all after the batch) so the differential harness exercises the P4-A1 class.

ADR0009:283-284: name the authoritative source of the 'complete point-read inventory' (archived position set from genesis plus live point reads), since the stock pool exposes no position enumeration and completeness cannot be proven from the contract alone.
principle_violations: ADR0009:284-285 claims the buffer 'reserves every still-withdrawable user claim' and ADR0008:284-285 requires 'any withdrawable unit must exit'; the aggregate hypothetical gate at 290-295 does not honor that for the last redeeming user at rounding boundaries (P4-A1).
